TCP congestion control is a protocol that is used to manage the flow of data packets in a network. It is designed to prevent congestion and ensure that data packets are delivered in a timely manner. The design of TCP congestion control involves several key components, including a congestion control algorithm, a congestion control table, and a congestion control queue.

The congestion control algorithm is responsible for detecting and managing congestion in the network. It uses a variety of techniques, such as rate limiting and priority scheduling, to ensure that data packets are delivered in a timely manner. The algorithm is designed to be efficient and scalable, so that it can handle a large number of data packets without slowing down the network.

The congestion control table is a data structure that is used to store information about the network. It is designed to keep track of the number of data packets that are currently in the network, as well as the number of data packets that are currently being sent. The table is updated in real-time, so that the congestion control algorithm can make informed decisions about how to manage the flow of data packets.

The congestion control queue is a data structure that is used to store data packets that are currently being sent. It is designed to keep track of the order in which the packets are being sent, as well as the order in which they are being received. The queue is updated in real-time, so that the congestion control algorithm can make informed decisions about how to manage the flow of data
